findings.reason: parseRange (range.js:115) now passes the raw string to hyphenReplace. range.js:503 builds `>=1.2.3+foo-0`, and parseComparator (range.js:258) strips re[t.BUILD]. BUILDIDENTIFIER allows '-', so the whole `+foo-0` is removed and the result is `>=1.2.3` instead of `>=1.2.3-0`.
findings.claim: With the up-front build-metadata strip removed and includePrerelease set, a hyphen range whose lower bound carries build metadata (e.g. `1.2.3+foo - 2.0.0`) loses its `-0` prerelease floor and rejects `1.2.3-alpha`.
findings.evidence: parseRange now goes straight to `range.replace(hr, hyphenReplace(this.options.includePrerelease))` without removing build metadata first. In hyphenReplace (line 503), `from = `>=${from}${incPr ? '-0' : ''}`` gets `from` as `1.2.3+build` and produces `>=1.2.3+build-0`. parseComparator (line 258) then runs `comp.replace(re[t.BUILD], '')`. BUILD matches `\+[a-zA-Z0-9-]+...`, which includes '-', so it strips `+build-0` and leaves `>=1.2.3` where the baseline gave `>=1.2.3-0`. This is the bleed the removed comment warned about ('strip build metadata so it can't bleed into the version').

findings.reason: re.js:144-149 allows BUILD only after a third component, so HYPHENRANGE (re.js:209) no longer matches once BUILDSTRIPRE is gone. The string is then split on spaces, and the lone `-` falls through parseComparator unchanged. That makes Comparator throw in strict mode, while the loose filter (range.js:143-146) drops it and ANDs the remaining contradictory comparators.
findings.claim: Hyphen ranges with a partial x-range endpoint carrying build metadata (e.g. `1.x+build - 2.0.0`) no longer parse: they throw in strict mode and become unsatisfiable in loose mode.
findings.evidence: In re.js:144-149, XRANGEPLAIN accepts BUILD only after a full patch component, so HYPHENRANGE (`^...$`) can't match `1.x+build - 2.0.0` now that the stripper is gone. The string is split on ' ', and `-` goes to `new Comparator('-')`, which throws in strict mode. In loose mode the COMPARATORLOOSE filter (lines 143-146) drops `-`, leaving `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0-0 2.0.0` ANDed together, which no version satisfies. Before the change, BUILDSTRIPRE removed `+build` first, so the input parsed as `>=1.0.0 <=2.0.0`.
